profile.headline: Python Core Developer and Principal Software Engineer at Anaconda
profile.summary:
* Extensive non-web Python development continuously since 2006.
* CPython core developer
* Close working knowledge of NAND flash technology, PCIe, and solid state drives.
* Over 5 years designing, implementing, and maintaining a distributed data migration platform.
* Over 5 years providing technical support for system administrators of virtual servers.
* Fluent in Spanish

Specialties: job processing, data migration, and system design

positions.title: Core Developer
positions.description:
As a Python core developer I work closely with other core developers and people in the Python community to make Python a better programming language.  This involves resolving bugs in the reference implementation (CPython) and adding (or rejecting) new features.  Work on Python centers on the bug tracker and various mailings lists.

My experience with Python core development began in July 2010, when I started following discussions on mailing lists in the pursuit of improving my Python proficiency and getting exposure to software development outside my professional domain.  Since then I have been able to participate in many discussions and in July 2011 became highly involved with Python's import system.  This led to becoming a core developer a year (and change) later.

The line between core development and the Python community at large is very thin.  In addition to work on Python itself I've also participated in various minor capacities in organizing and running the major annual Python technical conference, PyCon US.  This includes working on the program committee, reviewing and selecting talk proposals.  I've also presented talks at PyCon: 2 in 2012 and 1 in 2013 (as well as at the language summit in 2015 and 2018).

My work on Python includes the following:

* improvements to importlib
* improvements to the CPython runtime (including startup)
* added types.SimpleNamespace
* added the C implementation of OrderedDict
* proposals (https://www.python.org/dev/peps/)

positions.title: Software Engineer III (Lead Developer)
positions.description:
In this position I managed the internal systems for data migration operations for NTT/Verio.  Data migrations are run by a small and agile team that necessarily specializes in system development.  A key portion of my role was the design and implementation of both the libraries we used and the systems on which we relied.

The internal systems span across many more hosts than is manageable manually.  Each host fulfills at least one of the several roles that data migrations require, including central management, job execution, logging, access control, project management, release management, version control, and reporting.

Managing the internal systems is a comprehensive description.  Here are some of the activities:

* requirements gathering
* infrastructure design
* library framework design
* application library design
* scripting data migrations
* documentation
* library implementation
* regression testing
* packaging
* automated host configuration
* refactoring legacy code
* assess emerging technologies for applicability

We had a focus on APIs that allow external systems to tie in easily and especially helped our engineers keep a short turn-around on new projects.  This is essential for a small team like the one I was on.  Most of the design efforts centered on making our engineers more efficient.

Using these internal systems our team has been able to move hundreds of thousands of accounts between hosting platforms, applying complex transformations to both account configurations and content.  These hosting accounts have varied in capability from simple DNS point accounts to full-root virtual private servers.

As such the systems and libraries have had to be designed in such a way that they're efficient, highly maintainable, and easily adapted to handling new platforms (with different features and potentially new capabilities).  Early on we made a decision to use Python and a highly distributed design, both of which were key to meeting our objectives.

positions.title: Technical Support (for system administrators)
positions.description:
As a company Verio provides a vast array of products, particularly when I was there.  A core segment of those products centers on fully virtualized (albeit managed) Unix hosts, called VPS.  Each of these hosts is a full-root server (running virtualized on Verio-managed physical hosts) initialized with a standard image.  Consequently customers are the system administrator for their hosts.  Providing technical support for them was a challenging and rewarding proposition.

As a member of the technical support staff for the VPS products, my role was quite dynamic.  Here's some of what I did:

* Resolved technical issues for system administrators using the Verio VPS platform
* Educated system administrators in the use of several Unix flavors, including FreeBSD, Linux, and Solaris
* Likewise for a vast array of installable applications on those platforms
* Worked together with support team to solve technical issues on hosts, in its various incarnations
* Investigated and resolved security violations, including DoS attacks and rootkits
* Coached other team members
* Identified bugs in the platform and worked with the development team to resolve them

positions.title: Software Developer (Intern)
positions.description:
This was a part-time job while I was is school and a great opportunity to grow at an iconic institution in the computer world.

The job entailed, at first, maintaining legacy C code for a relatively successful suite of educational software used at elementary schools across the country called Schoolvista.  Here I was introduced to the product lifecycle, especially the long tail we call maintenance.  I became familiar with code control, QA processes, managing bug reports, and working with a team of other developers.

Part-way through my internship we switched to new development as we ported the existing products from stand-alone to network-based.  Reinventing the software involved taking the graphic/sound resources and logic from the existing codebase and duplicating them in a different environment.  At that time we chose Macromedia Director (and its Lingo scripting language), a predecessor to Flash, over Java for implementation.

The key aspect of the project was turning the different stand-alone applications into a single networked app.  Each of the original apps mapped to its own in the new design.  However, we had to manage dynamic deployment of these apps from a central networked host and conversely build them to communicate with that host once deployed.  This factored heavily into how we ported the resources and logic from the legacy code.

* Head TA during the transition of the intro programming course from Pascal to Java

volunteerExperience.companyName: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
volunteerExperience.description:
For 2 years I worked 24/7 alongside other missionaries (always in pairs) helping others and sharing our beliefs, particularly about Jesus Christ.  We took every opportunity to offer service, even if just a listening ear, to those in need.  We took seriously our mandate as representatives of Jesus Christ.

When anyone expressed a desire to learn more, my companion and I would teach them.  As teaching progressed we would invite them to live more Christ-like lives and eventually to join our church.  Much of our teaching closely involved local church members who would introduce their acquaintances to us, accompany us when teaching, and fellowship those being taught.

For part of my mission I led a small group of missionaries in our geographical area.  This involved providing counsel, coordinating efforts, and seeing to their temporal needs.  On the other side of my responsibilities, I worked with our mission leaders to be more effective as a group in helping those around us.  Our mission president led roughly 200 missionaries (a mix of young men and women and senior couples), so leadership was necessarily distributed.

My missionary experience provided many valuable lessons and helped develop important skills:

* Empathy and kindness.
* Standing by my convictions.
* Public speaking.
* Pushing outside my comfort zone.
* Dealing with adversity.
* Putting situations into perspective.
* Resolving interpersonal conflict.
* Coordinating efforts.
* Selflessness.
